Both assistants correctly apply the inclusion-exclusion principle to find the probability of the union (liking either color) and then calculate the complement (liking neither). Both arrive at the correct answer of 19% (or 0.19) with clear, step-by-step reasoning. Assistant A uses formal set notation and stays in percentage terms throughout, while Assistant B uses more conversational language and provides the answer in both decimal and percentage forms. Both explanations are accurate, complete, and equally helpful; the differences are purely stylistic with no meaningful advantage to either approach.
